notes: Half-life is the median age, in years, of a ruling's incoming citations from U.S. Reports opinions (citing year minus decision year; one citation per citing case). It is reported only for rulings cited at least 5 times. Data are right-censored: rulings decided recently have had little time to be cited, so their half-lives are biased low. To compare decades fairly, the by-decade chart counts only citations in each ruling's first 30 years, for rulings decided 1790 through 1984 with at least 10 such citations. Sudden deaths are rulings with at least 30 citations, 60 percent or more of them in the 20 years before the last citation, and none in the 25 or more years since. Immortals are rulings with at least 30 citations ranked by the span between first and last citing year. Only citing opinions spanning at least 2 pages count; one-page entries (orders, cert denials) are excluded from totals and tallied separately in orderCites, and only real opinions cited at least once are listed. Citations dated before the cited ruling are dropped as bad dates or mis-resolved cites. Citations come from CAP cites_to metadata, which only captures citations its parser recognized.
